extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors, media researchers, and policymakers interested in audience news habits
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for choosing and prioritizing news topics based on audience demographics, consumption patterns, and engagement drivers. Useful for newsroom editorial strategy, content planning, and research into newsworthiness by audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic targeting matters
rubrics_metrics.description: If editorial decisions reflect audience interest: demographic targeting matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different age groups prioritize different topics; newsrooms should calibrate coverage to the demographics they serve. Consider demographic composition when defining what is 'newsworthy' for your outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Younger Adults (under 30) — Less Likely to Get
rubrics_metrics.description: Younger adults are less likely to get government and politics, science and technology, and business and finance; slightly less likely to get sports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect lower baseline interest among under-30 audiences for these topics; boosting reach may require different formats or distribution strategies (e.g., social/video).

rubrics_metrics.name: Younger Adults (under 30) — More Likely to Get
rubrics_metrics.description: Younger adults are more likely to get entertainment news (32% vs. 13% for 65+), celebrity/pop culture, and lifestyle/wellness; sports about equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To engage younger audiences, prioritize entertainment, celebrity, and lifestyle content; tailor tone and platforms (short video, social-native formats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Older Adults (65+) — More Likely to Get
rubrics_metrics.description: Older adults (65+) are more likely to get government and politics, local news, business, and international news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlets targeting older audiences should emphasize politics, local reporting, business, and international affairs; distribution and format preferences may differ (e.g., traditional digital newsletters, TV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall follow frequency (attention level)
rubrics_metrics.description: 36% of people follow the news 'all or most of the time' (down from 51% in 2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declining continuous attention suggests lower baseline engagement; editors should account for weaker habitual news-following when planning content and measuring success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidental vs. intentional exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Young adults have more incidental exposure than intentional: 70% of young adults get political news incidentally vs. 30% intentionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because much of young audiences' news is incidental, optimize for discovery (strong headlines, visuals, social-friendly packaging) rather than assuming habitual readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform prevalence for news discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media news: TikTok 55%, X 57%, Truth Social 55% (platform-specific prevalence matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose platforms that reflect your target audience's habits; platform selection affects format, tone, and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-cutting interests (universal topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-cutting interests include weather, breaking emergencies, and local issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topics tend to engage across demographic groups and can be prioritized when broad reach or public service is the goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics that drive sustained news consumption: Politics and elections
rubrics_metrics.description: Politics and elections are top drivers of sustained news consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political coverage often retains audiences over time; invest in explanatory reporting and timely election coverage to sustain engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics that drive sustained news consumption: International conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: International conflicts are major drivers of sustained consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-depth, contextual reporting on international crises attracts and maintains audience attention; consider multimedia and expert analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics that drive sustained news consumption: Health (especially during crises)
rubrics_metrics.description: Health, notably during crises, drives sustained consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health reporting should balance immediacy with clarity and credibility; during crises, sustained audience interest rises sharply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics that drive sustained news consumption: Local news
rubrics_metrics.description: Local news is a key sustained-consumption topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust local reporting builds habitual audiences; prioritize community relevance and service journalism for retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics that drive sustained news consumption: Weather and natural events
rubrics_metrics.description: Weather and natural events consistently drive audience attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely, actionable weather coverage (alerts, forecasts) is both public-service oriented and audience-retentive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics that drive sustained news consumption: Sports
rubrics_metrics.description: Sports is among the top topics that sustain news consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sports coverage attracts loyal, recurring audiences; consider live updates, analysis, and community engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics that drive sustained news consumption: Celebrity / entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrity and entertainment content drive sustained consumption, especially among younger audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entertainment reporting can generate high engagement; adapt formats (video, short-form) to younger platforms to maximize reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics that drive sustained news consumption: Tech
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology is a sustained-interest topic, particularly for younger audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tech coverage should blend product-focused reporting with implications and explainers to retain informed audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics that drive sustained news consumption: Business and economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Business and the economy are among the topics that drive sustained consumption, especially for older audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic reporting that links national/global trends to audience finances and local impacts helps sustain interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics that drive sustained news consumption: Crime
rubrics_metrics.description: Crime reporting is a persistent driver of audience attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crime coverage should balance immediacy with context and ethical reporting standards; local crime often drives strong engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rising audience disengagement leads to engagement-friendly topic shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rising audience disengagement → newsrooms shift toward engagement-friendly topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that pursuit of engagement can change editorial priorities; weigh public-service obligations against audience-driven incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidental discovery increases importance of headline/visual quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidental discovery means headline/visual quality is more important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize headlines, thumbnails, and visuals for social and feed-based discovery to capture incidental audiences; prioritize clarity and attention-grabbing accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different newsrooms calibrate to different audience demographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Different newsrooms calibrate to different audience demographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial strategy should reflect an outlet's target demographic profile; consistent audience calibration improves relevance and retention.
